caption: Energy per run of the AI and the human implementation in each task. The bar gives the median and each point is one run.
Energy per run of the AI and the human implementation in each task. The bar gives the median and each point is one run.

Deviation of the energy of each run from its group mean against the GPU temperature at the start of the run, with a least-squares line per group and its R² in the panel title. The start temperature ranged from 34 to 44 °C and depends on the run before. It explains up to 85% of the variation within a group (ZAPBench human, +0.40% energy per °C).
Distribution of the energy per run in each task and treatment as a kernel density estimate. The ticks are the single runs and CV is the coefficient of variation.
Distribution of the energy per run in each task and treatment as a kernel density estimate. The ticks are the single runs and CV is the coefficient of variation.

Normal Q-Q plots of the CPU utilization and GPU utilization per run in each task, with the Shapiro-Wilk p-value of each treatment (in bold where p < 0.05). Implementations that do not use the GPU stay at 0% in every run and are not tested.
Normal Q-Q plots of the energy, execution time and memory increase per run in each task, with the Shapiro-Wilk p-value of each treatment (in bold where p < 0.05).

RQ2 per task, (a) execution time, (b) mean CPU utilization, (c) mean GPU utilization and (d) memory increase per run. The bar gives the median and each point is one run. The dashed line in (b) marks one of the 16 hardware threads at full load.

Energy per run against mean CPU utilization for each task and treatment, each panel on its own scales. The panel title gives Pearson's r or Spearman's rho with its 95% interval, and the line is a least-squares fit with its 95% band where the coefficient is Pearson's r.

Energy per run against mean GPU utilization for each task and treatment, each panel on its own scales. The panel title gives Pearson's r or Spearman's rho with its 95% interval, and the line is a least-squares fit with its 95% band where the coefficient is Pearson's r. scRNA-seq AI, scRNA-seq human, COVID-19 AI, COVID-19 human and GIFT-Eval AI do not use the GPU, stay at 0% in every run and are not shown.

Energy per run against memory increase for each task and treatment, each panel on its own scales. The panel title gives Pearson's r or Spearman's rho with its 95% interval, and the line is a least-squares fit with its 95% band where the coefficient is Pearson's r.

Energy per run against execution time for each task and treatment, each panel on its own scales. The panel title gives Pearson's r or Spearman's rho with its 95% interval, and the line is a least-squares fit with its 95% band where the coefficient is Pearson's r. Execution time is measured on the 0.2 s sampling grid of EnergiBridge. In scRNA-seq AI, scRNA-seq human and COVID-19 AI the run lengths fall on only 2 to 4 steps of this grid, and one sample more also adds one more interval of energy, so part of the correlation in these groups comes from the grid.
Correlation of the energy per run with each performance metric per task and treatment, with its 95% interval. Filled points are Pearson's r and open points Spearman's rho.
Correlation of the energy per run with each performance metric per task and treatment, with its 95% interval. Filled points are Pearson's r and open points Spearman's rho.

Ratio of the AI value to the human value of every variable in each task, on a log axis. A ratio below 1 means the AI value is lower, and an EQR below 1 that AI needs less energy for the quality it reaches. Mean power is not tested.
